name: Practiced caption compression
instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the line is compressed caption-native dialogue that assumes the drawing, omits explanation, and delivers one economical beat; do not judge whether the compression is effective.

name: Transcription artifacts
instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption exhibits catalog or transcription conventions such as lowercase starts, omitted terminal punctuation, ellipses, doubled hyphens, or spacing quirks; judge only visible text, not whether the caption is good.

name: Withholds the explanation the drawing seems to demand
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the caption declines to explain the odd thing in the drawing, and instead speaks as though it needed no explanation, leaving the reader to supply the logic. 10 = the strangeness is treated as entirely unremarkable; 0 = the caption spells out why the scene is the way it is.

name: Verbose conversational filler
instruction: Score the extent to which the caption uses spoken-style filler words (e.g., 'wow', 'sure', 'well', 'i guess') or conversational run-on phrasing to set up the punchline, adding words that do not change the core joke. Do not judge if the phrasing is good.

name: Topical Reference Self-Sufficiency
instruction: Score how well the caption's humor stands on its own without relying on a topical, cultural, or celebrity reference as the primary comedic engine. A 10 means the caption is fully self-sufficient—any reference present is incidental to a joke that works on its own terms, or no reference is needed at all. A 0 means the caption's entire comedic value depends on recognizing a specific topical reference and removing it leaves nothing.

name: Secondary-detail leverage
instruction: Score 10 when the humor depends on supporting props, background details, setting, or secondary characters as well as the central anomaly; score 0 when all such details are ignored.

name: Generic caption polish
instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the caption has compact, complete, immediately legible setup-punch packaging familiar from generic caption examples; do not judge whether it is funny or apt.

name: Bureaucratic or corporate jargon usage
instruction: Score the extent to which the caption uses specific corporate, bureaucratic, or administrative terminology (e.g., 'downsizing', 'litigation', 'human resources'). Do not judge if it fits the drawing well.

name: Explicitly names an object visible in the drawing
instruction: Score 0-10 for how many of the concrete objects, animals or settings visible in the cartoon are named in so many words in the caption. 10 = the caption names several of them explicitly; 0 = it names none. Count the naming only; do not judge whether naming them helps the joke.

name: Layered semantic convergence
instruction: Score 10 when two or more meanings converge cleanly on the pictured situation; score 0 when the line has only one thin, literal reading.

name: Extreme conversational brevity
instruction: Score the extent to which the caption is extremely short, abandoning any narrative setup to deliver a quick, blunt conversational response (e.g., 'chicken or rabbit'). Do not judge if brevity makes it a good caption.

name: Caption reframes what the drawing is a picture of
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the caption makes the reader see the whole drawing as a picture of a different situation from the one it obviously depicts. 10 = the scene is completely relocated by the line; 0 = the caption accepts the obvious reading of the scene and comments inside it.

name: Payoff surprise
instruction: Score 10 when the ending sharply redirects the reader toward an unexpected but coherent interpretation; score 0 when the punchline is an obvious first association or lacks a turn.

name: Generic-prior obvious idiom
instruction: Score the extent to which the caption relies on the single most obvious idiom, pun, or literal interpretation directly invited by the visual elements of the scene. Do not judge whether the joke is clever or well-executed.

name: Speaker-role fidelity
instruction: Score 10 when the line sounds natural for a particular depicted speaker given that character’s role and situation; score 0 when no plausible depicted speaker could say it.

name: Pun and idiom density
instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the caption relies on homophones, double meanings, transformed idioms, or concentrated wordplay; do not judge whether the wordplay is clever.

name: Petty-Stakes Emotional Grounding
instruction: Score how specifically and relatably a depicted character is invested in a small, human-scale concern—petty grievance, minor inconvenience, domestic anxiety, social embarrassment—rather than the grand absurdity of the scene. A 10 means the character's emotional investment is vivid, relatable, and comically disproportionate to the surreal situation. A 0 means no specific emotional investment is conveyed.

name: Conversational punch timing
instruction: Score 10 when the wording has a natural setup and lands its strongest turn at the end; score 0 when it is awkwardly phrased, overexplained, or lacks a punch.

name: Topical news cycle reference
instruction: Score the extent to which the caption explicitly names or directly references a specific contemporary real-world entity, person, product, or event (e.g., 'n95 mask', 'stimulus', 'trump'). Do not judge if the reference is funny or apt, only how specific and time-bound the named entity is.

name: Non-template angle
instruction: Score 10 when the association is surprising and individualized rather than a stock response; score 0 when it uses the first cliché suggested by the image.

name: House-style tonal register
instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses plain, restrained, everyday conversational diction and understated social framing; do not judge whether that register suits the cartoon.

name: Freshness over cliché
instruction: Score 10 when a familiar phrase, reference, or association is materially twisted into a new comic idea; score 0 when it reproduces a stock expression with minimal alteration.

name: Number of words in the caption
instruction: Score 0-10 inversely with the caption's raw length in words: 10 = five words or fewer, 0 = more than twenty-five words, scaling in between. Count words only; do not judge whether the length suits the joke.

name: Deadpan Underreaction To Surreal Danger
instruction: Score 10 if the speaker treats a highly dangerous, bizarre, or impossible situation as a mundane, bureaucratic, or trivial inconvenience. Score 0 if the speaker reacts with shock or directly addresses the impossibility of the situation.

name: Setup-to-Payoff Register Shift
instruction: Score how effectively the caption's opening words set up one expectation—emotional, tonal, or topical—and then deliver the payoff in a deliberately different register. A 10 means the gap between setup and payoff registers is wide and surprising yet perfectly coherent. A 0 means the setup leads predictably and linearly to its conclusion with no tonal pivot.
